### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**10** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 301b7c11c5f24a52db706f9016155293c066756d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8600f655b8b7a319c81129e750648c76b6decb66` — the merge of head `b2f55b4eb7e8e029c1df489121a97f18c7814370` into base `301b7c11c5f24a52db706f9016155293c066756d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 8600f655b8b7a319c81129e750648c76b6decb66 && git checkout 8600f655b8b7a319c81129e750648c76b6decb66
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 301b7c11c5f24a52db706f9016155293c066756d b2f55b4eb7e8e029c1df489121a97f18c7814370 && git checkout -B drift-repro 301b7c11c5f24a52db706f9016155293c066756d && git merge --no-ff b2f55b4eb7e8e029c1df489121a97f18c7814370

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 301b7c11c5f24a52db706f9016155293c066756d
```

## 席位核对

**L1 review · REWORK (paper only; the code is accepted)** · Head-sha: `b2f55b4eb7e8e029c1df489121a97f18c7814370` · card #34672 (insert half, narrowing) · read 2026-11-18T02:26Z

This is a full review: there is no earlier L1 record. I read the whole diff from merge-base `eb7b09d4` (11 files, +450 / -103), plus:
- claim 6962699354;
- premise reading 6963917179;
- amendment 6963962011 (route A, conditions 1–5);
- dev report 6967101808.

The history has 3 commits and 2 pure main merges, and nothing was rewritten.

**The lock (`engine-top-level.ts`).**
- `withSummaryRollUpsReadonly` is now the single way the roll-up lock is spelled, and both static-`readonly` views read it.
- **Create side.** `insertStaticReadonlySubject` applies it *before* `staticReadonlyInsertSubject` judges the schema, so the `sys_` and `managedBy` exclusions still hold. The pre-hook withhold and the post-hook strip read the same subject, so `beforeInsert` is never handed a value that will not be stored.
- **Update side.** `updateStaticReadonlySubject` reads the same helper, so it answers as before.
- **Exemption.** `isSystem` runs none of these passes: seed loads, installs, historical imports and the recompute keep their value. The rename `summaryFieldsLockedOnUpdate` → `summaryFieldsLockedOnWrite` has no caller outside `objectql/src`.

**The seed (`engine-insert.ts`, condition 1).**
- `staticReadonlyCreateStrip` re-runs `initializeSummaryFields` over the stripped row and copies the result back for taken keys that are still `null`. The column then starts at `0` for `count`/`sum` and stays empty for `min`/`max`/`avg`, the same as a create that never named the field. The `readonly: true` → `null` defect is gone.
- The re-seed sits inside the branch that runs only after the re-default's permission resolution succeeded. On failure the row comes back as it arrived, as before.

**Condition 2 (Console).** The Console sends no summary value on create: `sanitizeFormData` drops `COMPUTED_FIELD_TYPES`, and its two existing pins pass. The schemaless `customFields` edge is now dropped by the engine.

**Condition 4 (pins).**
- Each forced edit states its new expectation. Two examples: the batch seed case and the "author supplied" case now write as `isSystem`, with a new ordinary-caller case that drops the value and seeds the column; the REST blank-typed cases expect `droppedFields: [{ … fields: ['f_summary'], reason: 'readonly' }]`.
- 14 engine pins cover the REST shape, batch, strict refusal, `readonly: true`, the `isSystem` exemption and `preserveAudit` with no exemption. There are 3 REST import pins.
- The body reports two ablations: lock off turns 16 red and re-seed off turns 10 red, with the references staying green. I did not re-run them.
- `fields.mdx` describes both verbs.

**Paper.**
- **Changeset levels.** `fix(objectql)!` is a patch, with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and ADR-0087 `not-required`. Check Changeset's LEVEL AXIS and the ADR-0087 step pass at this head.
- **Migration line (condition 3).** It names REST, import and MCP, with `isSystem` as the server-side route.
- **Battery (condition 5).** It ran on this exact head, `b2f55b4e`: 4072/68, `VERDICT 0`.
- **Governance.** Not governed.

**Gates at this head (latest attempt per check):** 1 failed (Check Changeset), 15 success, 15 skipped, 21 still running. Check Changeset is red only on the foreign-changeset rule (#17712) for `.changeset/34672-summary-readonly-on-update.md`, the declared DELIBERATE CORRECTION; every other axis in that job is green. The correction is the right class. #34752's pending note says "a create keeps a value sent for a summary field", and this PR makes that false, so restoring it would ship a false sentence. Both rewritten sentences are quoted in the body. Per the gate's own text, the seat confirms it by its record.

### Should-fix (blocks; paper only)

- **S1: two paths sit outside the amended surface.** Amendment 6963962011 lists `packages/objectql/src/**` and its tests, four named pin files (the only `packages/rest` one is `rest-data-blank-typed-value.test.ts`), `fields.mdx` and "one changeset". The diff also touches:
  - `packages/rest/src/import-summary-update-lock-34672.test.ts` (+73: the import create pins);
  - `.changeset/34672-summary-readonly-on-update.md` (the deliberate correction; the body cites the dispatch order, not the claim).

  Both are justified. A claim amendment on #34672 naming the two paths, as on #35034 and #35080, puts that on the record the land gate reads. Once it is posted, I will turn this into a same-head ACCEPT.

**Owed, for the seat:**
1. The narrowing contract review, at tier.
2. Your record confirming the DELIBERATE CORRECTION of #34752's update note. Check Changeset stays red until then.

This comment readies, queues and arms nothing.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b2f55b4eb7e8e029c1df489121a97f18c7814370`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-summary-update-lock.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-rollup.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-blank-typed-value-door.test.ts, packages/rest/src/import-summary-update-lock-34672.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-data-blank-typed-value.test.ts + read, not reviewed: packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-validate.ts, packages/rest/src/import-prepare.ts, packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-data-writes.ts, packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-readonly-flow-writes.ts; the two changesets and content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx read only for the migration line and the deliberate correction
Security-touching: yes

PR #35089 (card #34672, insert half, route A). Net diff read as `eb7b09d4d2..b2f55b4eb7` (the head is a merge of `main` at `eb7b09d4d2`): 11 files, +450 / -103, the same list GitHub serves for the PR. Inputs: the card body and all 17 comments, the PR body, file list and comments, the check-runs on the head (read 2026-11-18T02:35Z), the npm registry metadata of `@objectstack/objectql`.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each read in the code at the head:

1. **A non-system create no longer stores a caller's value for a roll-up `summary` field: right.** `insertStaticReadonlySubject` (`engine-top-level.ts`) now judges `withSummaryRollUpsReadonly(schema)`, so every `type === 'summary'` field reads as `readonly: true` for the three create-side static passes that share that one view: the pre-hook withhold (`withholdInsertReadonlyFromHooks`), the post-hook strip (`engine-insert.ts`, `staticReadonlyCreateStrip`) and the `insert`-mode preview (`engine-validate.ts`). All three sit behind `!context?.isSystem`. Every create door ends in `engine.insert` (`insertMany` is `insert` with `__partialRowErrors`), so no door is left on the old answer.
2. **The taken column starts at the empty-child-list seed: right.** `staticReadonlyCreateStrip` re-runs `initializeSummaryFields` over the stripped row after the re-default and copies back only taken keys that are still null. `initializeSummaryFields` seeds `0` for `count` / `sum` and nothing for `min` / `max` / `avg`, and never overwrites a non-null value, so a non-summary taken key and a taken key with its own `defaultValue` are untouched. The seed is an in-memory fill, no query.
3. **The declared `readonly: true` roll-up no longer lands null on such a create (route condition 1): right.** Same four lines; pinned by "the declared readonly: true roll-up alone lands 0, not null", which asserts the driver's create payload.
4. **`isSystem` is the only exemption: right.** Seed loads, package installs and `@objectstack/verify` fixtures write under `SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT` (`isSystem: true`); `treatAsHistorical` is refused for every non-system caller at the import doors (`importControlOptOutRefusal`, `import-prepare.ts:431-437`), so a historical import is a system write. `preserveAudit` without `isSystem` gets nothing, as for every other read-only column on create (the 2026-08-08 ruling in `rule-validator.ts`), and is pinned.
5. **`sys_` objects and the platform-internal `managedBy` buckets stay outside the create lock: right as declared.** The flag is added before `staticReadonlyInsertSubject` judges the schema, so its two object-level exclusions hold. This leaves the create side narrower than the update half (which locks every object); the changeset says so, and no platform object declares a `summary` field at this head.
6. **The update half answers as before: right.** `updateStaticReadonlySubject` reads the same helper; the result is the schema with the same fields flagged, `organization_id` removed under the same condition.
7. **Public surface: none moved.** `summaryFieldsLockedOnUpdate` becomes `summaryFieldsLockedOnWrite`; it is a module export of `engine-top-level.ts` with no reference outside `packages/objectql/src` and none in `src/index.ts`. No spec file, baseline, drop reason or error code changes.

What an existing caller sees, door by door (drop unless stated; refusal only under the in-process `strictReadonlyWrites` option, which no REST, MCP, import or flow door passes):

| Door | Before | At this head | Told? |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST `POST /api/v1/data/:object` | stored as sent | dropped; `0` for `count`/`sum`, empty for `min`/`max`/`avg` | `droppedFields`, reason `readonly` (pinned over HTTP + SQLite) |
| REST batch / `createMany` / composite | stored as sent | same | the same `createData` / `insertMany` report (read, not pinned for a summary) |
| Import `insert`, and the rows an `upsert` creates | stored as sent | same | per-row `droppedFields`, dry run and commit (pinned) |
| MCP `create_record`, HTTP transport | stored as sent | same | the protocol's create answer carries `droppedFields` (read, not pinned) |
| MCP `create_record`, stdio bridge | stored as sent | same | not told: see N1 |
| Flow `create_record`, not run as system | stored as sent | same | `droppedFields` and a warning on the node output |
| Flow `create_record`, `runAs: 'system'` | stored | stored | n/a |
| Public form submit (anonymous) | stored as sent | same | not told: the answer is the id only (see N2) |
| A hook's or other server code's insert without `isSystem` | stored as sent | same | server WARN, `onFieldsDropped` if passed |
| Seed loads, package installs, historical imports, the recompute | stored | stored | n/a |
| `insert`-mode preview (`validate`) | no drop reported | reports the drop | pinned |

Forced pin edits, each read against its old text: none is weakened to green.
- `engine-summary-update-lock.test.ts`: "INSERT is not narrowed" is inverted, same payload, now asserting the report and the stored `0`.
- `summary-rollup.test.ts`: the two "author supplied" cases keep their assertions under `isSystem: true`, and a new ordinary-caller case asserts the opposite (`0` and `0`), so both sides of the boundary are pinned where one was.
- `engine-blank-typed-value-door.test.ts`: the insert cases now assert `f_summary` is absent from the driver payload, a stricter statement than the old null; every other typed column keeps its assertion.
- `rest-data-blank-typed-value.test.ts`: the fixture seed moves to `isSystem` (the one writer that may set it), and the valid-value case asserts `droppedFields` and a null column, with the reason stated (that fixture's roll-up declares no `summaryOperations`, so nothing seeds it).
- New: 14 engine cases and 3 REST cases, covering both seed families, batch, `insertMany`, strict refusal, preview, the hook view, children stored before the parent, `isSystem`, `preserveAudit`, `sys_`.

Gate verdicts on the head at 02:35Z: 26 success, 15 skipped, 1 failure, 11 with no conclusion yet. The failure is `Check Changeset`, and its log shows one red step only, the foreign-changeset rule on `.changeset/34672-summary-readonly-on-update.md`; the same job prints the level axis, the ADR-0087 registration and the no-major check green. `Test Core (1/10)` to `(10/10)` and `Type Check · workspace` were still running: this record does not answer them, and the landing reads their conclusions. `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, the lint families and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/objectql`, `fix(objectql)!` with a BREAKING banner: matches what the diff publishes. One package's behaviour changes, no schema key, accepted metadata value, export or baseline moves, and the `Check Changeset` level axis reads it so on this head ("a non-protocol change at `patch`, its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition untouched by the level").

Clause-②: no (narrowing). Right: a create that stored a caller's value now drops it, nothing is widened.
Metadata-protocol: none. Right: nothing an author writes in metadata is accepted, refused or read differently; the same line was judged right for the update half.
ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: right, nothing stored is rewritten and the fix is one sentence, which the body carries.

The migration line is present and names REST, import and MCP clients and the `isSystem` route for server code. It is accurate for what the engine does; its "reported in `droppedFields`" is not true of one MCP transport (N1), and the door list omits two doors that are narrowed too (N2).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in report 6967101808.
- SQL push-down: no new id materialisation, read or in-app join. The re-seed is `initializeSummaryFields`, a pure fill over the row in hand.
- Flag, `check-empty-changeset` red by design: answered, see the confirmation line under ④.
- Flag, `check:type-check-debt` NOT MEASURED locally: answered by CI, `Type Check · debt ledger` is success on this head.
- Flag, overlap with #33849 (Version Packages) on the corrected changeset: accepted, that PR is regenerated from `main`. One consequence the seat should hold: the corrected note says the create side is narrowed "in the same release". That is true only if this PR lands before a release consumes the update note. If a release is cut first, the edit to that file has nothing to apply to and the create changeset stands alone, which it can.
- Flag, deviations (battery run before `pr_create`; the local merge message amended before its first push; the `(wip)` subject left in history): no contract effect.
- Flag, out-of-scope note (a Console form built only from inline `customFields` sanitizes without a schema): harmless as the dev says, the engine now drops and reports it. Not reviewed: no `ui/` path is in the diff.
- Flag, file surface: the two paths L1 found outside the amended claim are inside it since amendment 6967174314.
- Flag, the ruling of record: amendment 6963962011 records route A as the seat's ruling, relayed, where the seat's earlier note 6949162788 said the insert half needed a maintainer ruling. ④ below finds the narrowing enforces what the spec already states, which is the ground the amendment gives. This record is not a maintainer ruling and does not stand in for one; whether the seat's word is enough for this route is the seat's to cite, not escalated here.
- `Security-touching: yes` is meant. The changed hunks extend the server-enforced static `readonly` write lock, which `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx` and the authz conformance matrix (`readonly-static-write`) class as security enforcement, and they restate its `isSystem` exemption. Nothing here is an undisclosed mechanism: the card is public and describes it.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing makes the spec's own statement real; it takes no declared capability away.** On `main` the published spec lists `summary` in `COMPUTED_VALUE_TYPES`, "Server-computed types: never client-written" (`field-value.zod.ts`), and `FieldSchema.summaryOperations` says the engine recomputes the value. No ADR and no spec text declares a starting value. What said otherwise was a code comment (the #6014 note in `rule-validator.ts`), a descriptive "Unchanged ... stored as sent" line in older changelogs, and the fields.mdx sentence #34752 added on 2026-11-17, which has not shipped in a release. The two uses the note protected, seed data and historical imports, write as the system principal and keep their value. The only caller left on the old answer was the card's own actor.

**Dropped, not refused, is the card's answer.** The card's Expected reads "the write is dropped and reported in `droppedFields`, as already happens for formula and readonly fields"; route A adds the seed. The diff does exactly that, through the existing strip, with reason `readonly` and no new code path for reporting.

Tried to break it, in the code:
- A second view that could disagree: there is none. The withhold, the strip and the preview read `insertStaticReadonlySubject`; a hook is shown the seed and the stored row carries the seed (pinned).
- The #6014 hazard (a strip that leaves null behind a successful write): closed by the re-seed, and the ablation in the PR body turns the pin red without it.
- The re-seed overwriting something it should not: it writes only taken keys that are null after the re-default, so a field `defaultValue` and a hook's own write (kept by `hookWrittenKeys`) survive.
- A failed permission resolution in the re-default returns the row as it arrived, caller's value included, but with `error` set: `insert` throws or culls that row and `validate` throws, so that row is never stored.
- A historical import losing its totals: not reachable, `treatAsHistorical` is system-only at both import doors.
- A restore from the recycle bin re-creating a row with its totals: not a create (ADR-0148 D2), it does not pass this strip.
- A parent created after its children: it starts at `0`, not the true sum, until the next child write. That is the answer any create that names no roll-up already gets, and the changeset says the column "starts as if no value had been sent". Not a regression of this diff.

The rewritten #6014 note agrees with the code it describes: `summary` stays out of `RUNTIME_OWNED_FIELD_TYPES`, for the two reasons it gives (that strip honours `preserveAudit`, and it runs after the seed pass).

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits (none affects the engine's answer or the contract; each is prose or a follow-up outside this diff):

- N1 (nit) — The changeset's migration line and fields.mdx say an MCP create reports the drop in `droppedFields`. The stdio bridge (`packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`, `create`) calls `engine.insert` with no `onFieldsDropped` and answers `{ ...data, ...written }`, so on that transport the caller is not told, and where the write result omits the key (a `min` / `max` / `avg` roll-up on a driver that returns the row it was handed) the answer can echo the caller's value. This predates the PR and is the same for every `readonly` column and for the update half; the PR widens how often it is met. Fix on the prose faces (say "on the HTTP transport"), or leave it and file a follow-up card for the bridge.
- N2 (nit) — The changeset's door list omits two doors that are narrowed with the rest: the public form submit (`packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts`, anonymous, the answer is the id only, so the drop is not shown to the submitter) and a caller's `overrides` on clone (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-data-crud.ts`, which reports the drop through the same listener as a create). Both end in the engine's insert. Prose only.
- N3 (nit) — Follow-up, outside this diff: `packages/lint/src/validate-readonly-flow-writes.ts` knows only a declared `readonly: true`, so a user-run flow whose `create_record` or `update_record` sets a roll-up gets no lint finding although the engine now drops the value on both verbs; and the static `readonly` section of `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx` does not name the implicit roll-up lock. Both gaps date from the update half.

Deliberate correction confirmed: `.changeset/34672-summary-readonly-on-update.md` (the pending note of #34752). It is unpublished: the file on `main` is still blob `c33d0f79e0`, added by `a825152ea7` on 2026-11-17, and the newest `@objectstack/objectql` on npm is 18.5.0, published 2026-11-15; `packages/objectql/CHANGELOG.md` at this head carries no entry for it. The PR body declares the correction, names the note and quotes both rewritten sentences. Judged sentence by sentence at this head:
- Old: "An import with `writeMode: 'upsert'` drops the value on the rows it updates and keeps it on the rows it creates." False at this head: the created row's value is dropped and reported (pinned by the upsert case in `import-summary-update-lock-34672.test.ts`).
- New: "An import with `writeMode: 'upsert'` drops the value on the rows it updates; the rows it creates are covered by the create-side entry (`34672-summary-readonly-on-create`)." True.
